title: Senate Committee Hears Testimony Alleging Russian Organized Crime Activity
description_short: CNN reported testimony about Russian organized crime at a 1996 Senate hearing; the report does not establish the Trump or Mogilevich claims in the supplied headline.
description_medium: CNN reported on May 16, 1996, that the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee heard former Mafia figure Michael Franzese allege that Russian mob members were expanding internationally with Italian Mafia help and using the United States as a base. CNN also described testimony from other witnesses and DEA officials. The report does not establish a committee finding about Semion Mogilevich or connect the hearing to Donald Trump.
description_long: On May 16, 1996, CNN reported testimony heard by the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee about Russian organized crime in the United States. Former Mafia capo Michael Franzese told senators that Russian mob members were working with the Italian Mafia and using the United States as a base. CNN quoted him describing large cash payments and reported that he alleged Russian mob members devised gasoline-tax fraud schemes. The article also reported that Anthony “Gas Pipe” Casso, testifying behind a screen, said he had ordered a murder to protect a criminal racket; that is an allegation attributed to his testimony. CNN added that Drug Enforcement Administration officials told the hearing Russian and Italian groups were moving into drug deals. This is a report about general organized-crime testimony, not a committee finding about the Semion Mogilevich Organization. The accessible article does not mention Mogilevich or Donald Trump. TrumpFile’s separate page asserts that the hearing recognized Mogilevich’s organization and links the story to Trump through associates, but the cited Senate PDF could not be text-extracted in this review, and those assertions are not independently established here. The narrower event has no demonstrated Trump action or relationship, so it should be considered for exclusion from a Trump-event collection.
date_precision: TrumpFile page gives May 15; CNN posted May 16 and describes testimony Wednesday; underlying Senate PDF not text-extracted.

title: Internal Draft: Trump’s May 2025 Tariff Claims About the Economy
description_short: Internal draft: the supplied record attributes a “saved the economy” claim to Trump in May 2025, but gives no verified date or transcript.
description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Trump repeatedly said tariffs had saved the U.S. economy in May 2025 and contrasts the claim with economic forecasts. The packet does not identify a dated statement or transcript for that wording and combines several forecasts, market changes, and credit-rating developments. The absolute phrase “every major economist” is not supported.
description_long: This internal draft preserves the supplied allegation that Trump made repeated May 2025 claims that tariffs had saved the U.S. economy, but the record provides no dated statement or transcript for the quoted wording. The supplied synopsis also groups together statements, forecasts, market moves, credit-rating changes, and predictions about prices and GDP without identifying the source or date for each. A separate official May 30 transcript reviewed for comparison records Trump’s remarks at U.S. Steel’s Irvin Works. In that passage, he said, “We saved the company,” while describing tariffs and the steel producer. That company-specific statement is distinct from the asserted claim about saving the national economy and cannot verify it. This draft therefore attributes the original allegation to the supplied record, removes the absolute assertion that every major economist disagreed, and does not present the quote or economic effects as established. The stored May 1 date is only a month placeholder, not a confirmed statement date. The exact wording, date, and scope of the claimed statement remain unverified, so this copy is not eligible for publication.
date_precision: May 2025 only; May 1 is a storage placeholder from the frozen record, not a verified statement date.

title: Internal Draft: Alleged Federal Database Tracking Anti-Trump Posts
description_short: Internal draft: the supplied record alleges a federal database tracked posts critical of Trump; the packet contains no source establishing that database.
description_medium: The supplied record alleges that the Trump administration created a federal database to track social media posts critical of Trump, using platform data and government tools. It provides no database name, agency record, source URL, or verified date. A separate report about ICE monitoring social media for immigration-enforcement leads concerns a different proposal and does not substantiate this allegation.
description_long: This internal draft preserves the supplied allegation that the Trump administration launched a federal database to monitor social media posts critical of Trump. The frozen record says the system drew on multiple platforms and government surveillance tools, was described as a national-security measure, and targeted domestic political critics; it also alleges civil-liberties objections and a chilling effect. The packet names no database, responsible office, procurement record, legal filing, quoted official, or source URL that establishes those details. They remain unverified allegations, not findings. A separate WIRED report published October 3, 2025, describes ICE’s request for information about contractors who would monitor social platforms and prepare immigration-enforcement leads. WIRED says the initiative was still at the request-for-information stage. Its later date, ICE enforcement purpose, and proposed contractor operation differ from the alleged March 2025 database aimed at domestic critics, so it does not verify or replace that event. This draft does not assert that the database existed, that named officials directed it, or that a chilling effect occurred. March 1 is only the frozen record’s month placeholder; no launch date is established. Publication remains ineligible pending evidence for the central allegation and its details.
date_precision: March 2025 only; March 1 is a frozen-record placeholder, not a verified launch date.
